meta.rule: Only what you have proven you own and confirmed is scanned.

rule: Scanning your external surface is active scanning, so Vedette sets two conditions. First, you prove ownership: a domain with a DNS TXT record (re-checked right before every scan), a public IP only when this box itself reaches the Internet through it (the box finds it by itself and renews it each time it sees it; 30 days after it last saw it, it expires). Second, an administrator with two-step sign-in confirms that your company owns it and that the scan is authorized: the first Scan now of a target records that confirmation, with the exact sentence shown beside the button. Until then the button stays locked for everyone else. Every verification and scan is written to the audit log.

risky.voip: Phone systems (SIP) are scanned all day for toll fraud: attackers guess extension passwords and make paid calls on your bill.
risky.remote: Remote access is the most attacked way in: attackers guess passwords and use known flaws to log in.
risky.files: File sharing should never face the Internet: ransomware gangs scan for it.
risky.database: Databases should never face the Internet: they are scanned for weak or missing passwords to steal or wipe the data.
risky.control: This service controls the device or the containers on it: whoever reaches it can take the device over.
risky.camera: Camera recorders are taken over in bulk for botnets, often with factory passwords.

verify.dnsIntro: Add a TXT record to the DNS of {{value}}. Do it where you manage the domain (your registrar, Cloudflare, or whoever hosts your DNS).
verify.dnsHint: This record only proves you control the DNS. It gives Vedette no other access. Paste the value without quotes. If your DNS provider appends the domain to the Name field automatically, type just @. DNS usually updates within minutes, can take up to 72 hours (as in Google domain verification guidance). Keep the record until Vedette confirms verification; you can delete it afterwards.

verify.paused: Scans paused: the box no longer reaches the Internet through this IP (last seen {{time}}). Scanning resumes when the box goes out through it again. Select Verify again to check now.
verify.ipExpired: The box has not seen this IP for 30 days, so it cannot be scanned. It becomes valid again once the box goes out through it: turn on auto-detect, or route the box through this IP (for example switch WAN) and verify again.
verify.ipRecheckHint: Works only while this box currently reaches the Internet through {{value}}. Verify again runs a full check: the box asks checkip.amazonaws.com, icanhazip.com and ifconfig.me/ip over 5 rounds on new connections (15 requests), so any IP behind a load balancer is found. It renews the IP for 30 days and uses one of the 10 attempts an hour.

Names hosted elsewhere are reached over the Internet, but the box's own public IP is reached through your router (NAT loopback), so what it shows can differ from what the Internet sees: a router may show its own login page only to the inside, and a router without NAT loopback shows nothing.

help.summary: How the box finds its IPs
help.how: The box asks three public "what is my IP" services over HTTPS: checkip.amazonaws.com (AWS), icanhazip.com (Cloudflare) and ifconfig.me/ip (Google Cloud). It accepts an IP only when at least two of them return the same one, so one wrong answer is not enough. A full check does this in 5 rounds on new connections (15 requests), so several IPs behind a load balancer all show up. The first check after install, Detect now and Verify again are full checks. The automatic checks after that ask each service once (3 requests).
help.result: Each IP the box sees is added or renewed for 30 days from that moment. An IP expires only when the box has not seen it for 30 days.
help.why: You cannot type an IP. Only an address the box really uses proves it belongs to your network, so nobody can verify someone else's address.
help.refuse: Private, reserved and shared carrier (CGNAT, 100.64.0.0/10) addresses are refused, because scanning them could hit other people.
help.limit: Detect now, Verify again and the DNS Check of a domain share 10 attempts per hour. Automatic checks do not use them: they can run as often as every minute, and a full check runs at most once an hour by itself. Every change is written to the audit log.

greenbone.title: Optional deep scan: Greenbone (OpenVAS)
greenbone.description: Greenbone is a free vulnerability scanner that runs as its own containers next to Vedette. When it is on, each scan of the box's own verified public IP ends with a Greenbone scan of that IP. Off by default.

stateText.off: Greenbone is off. Scans do not use it.
stateText.starting: Greenbone is starting. The first start downloads its images (about 9 GB).
stateText.ready: Greenbone is ready. The next scan of an IP of this box uses it.

greenbone.loading: Greenbone is loading its feed (first time takes about 2 hours)
greenbone.what: It looks at your public IP from outside without logging in, with Greenbone's "Full and fast" tests minus brute force, default accounts, denial of service and generic web application scanning, and with safe checks on.
greenbone.apart: Its results are shown in their own section of each scan. They never replace or hide what Vedette found by version, and finding nothing is not proof that nothing is affected.
greenbone.weekly: While it is on, Vedette updates Greenbone's feed once a week, never during a scan, and only with 60 GB free.
greenbone.offKeeps: Turning it off stops its containers and keeps its images and data, so turning it on again does not download them again.
greenbone.feedNever: Not yet: the first one is a week after it is turned on
greenbone.needs: Needs about 50 GB of disk and about 2 hours to load Greenbone's feed the first time. The box must have at least 8 GB of memory and 60 GB free.
greenbone.heldOn: It is still turned on from before: turn it off to stop its containers. Its data is kept.
greenbone.toastOn: Greenbone is starting. Loading its feed takes about 2 hours the first time.
greenbone.toastOff: Greenbone is off. Its data is kept.

results.title: Greenbone results (unauthenticated, QoD ≥ 70)
results.header: Greenbone looked at this IP from outside without logging in. Finding nothing is not proof the services are not affected (distributions backport fixes). For the same reason, on Ubuntu or Debian a result read from a version banner can be a false positive, so Vedette's own package-based result wins when both exist.
results.caption: What Greenbone reported on this IP
results.noneTitle: Greenbone reported no high or medium result with QoD 70 or more
results.noneBody: That is one outside look without logging in, not proof that the services are not affected. The exploited CVEs above still stand.

results.notRunBody: Greenbone is not set up for this scan.
results.notesHeader: Greenbone's Low results are hardening suggestions, such as weak SSH settings or TCP timestamps. They are not alerts and are not counted anywhere.
results.notesCaption: Greenbone's hardening notes on this IP
